title: Peptide Bioregulators in Space Medicine: A Systematic Analysis of Perspectives Based on Ground‑Based Models
content: Long-duration space missions expose crews to multiple stressors that cause persistent pathological changes, including spaceflight-associated neuro-ocular syndrome (SANS), muscle and bone atrophy, and immune dysfunction. Existing countermeasures do not fully eliminate these risks. This systematic review evaluates the potential of peptide bioregulators as a novel preventive strategy against these disorders. We conducted a systematic literature review in PubMed, Scopus, and the NASA Human Research Roadmap (1990–2025). Preclinical and clinical data show that peptide bioregulators have tissue-specific effects on key target organs, exhibiting retinoprotective, osteoprotective, myoprotective, immunomodulatory, and antioxidant activities. While limited by the lack of in-flight studies, peptide bioregulators could potentially increase crew resistance to spaceflight stressors. They represent a promising adjunctive strategy that warrants targeted in-flight testing for future missions.
